liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Friend Of The Devil** (2 other sources): This version has different lyrics than usual [2][3]
- **Wake Up Little Susie** (1 review): Setlist includes 1950s and 1960s covers such as this one [14]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Where the show picks up, including a big China Cat tease [14]
- **Viola Lee Blues** (1 review): The Viola Lee Blues into The Eleven segment is singled out as especially sweet [10]
- **The Seven** (1 review): The Seven into Cumberland Blues pairing is a real treat [11]
- **He Was a Friend of Mine** (1 review): Quite good once the sound is tolerated; reviewer imagines a studio version fitting on Workingman's Dead [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Wake Up Little Susie**: rare: 9 archived performances [21]
- **wanna hear Pigpen?**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]
- **Katie Mae**: rare: 10 archived performances [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-03-21.late.aud.lee.pcrp.21779.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 125 min; rated 3.92/5 by 13 [1]
- **gd70-03-21.late.aud.5316.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 16 songs; 105 min; rated 4.29/5 by 7 [5]. Said about its sound: Good audience recording for its time, with solid tuning segment [14]
- **gd70-03-21.early.aud.5315.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 15 songs; 74 min; rated 4/5 by 7 [7]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds it a nice-sounding tape for any year, not just an early one; Right channel wavers heavily and the mix is very bassy; sound quality poor; Mediocre recording with muddy vocals [9][10][11]
- **gd70-03-21.early.lee.pcrp.20184.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 10 songs; 75 min; rated 4.42/5 by 19 [8]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording sounds great for 1970 and should be played loud; Real nice-sounding audience recording, as if made recently [13][16]

## Around the show

- Audience members can be heard yelling out remarks throughout the recording [9]
- Jerry's playing roams everywhere all night, and there are nice harmonies late in the show [11]
- The extremely restless crowd chanted for others to sit down and shut up [1]
- Wake Up Little Susie was played in response to an audience request [2]
- Catfish was advertised on the bill and may have played an opening set before the late show [2]
- Wake Up Little Susie was played in response to an audience request [3]
- The set was split into electric and acoustic portions; Catfish was advertised on the bill [3]
- The set had electric and acoustic sections, with Friend Of The Devil through Katie Mae acoustic [5]
- Recommends also getting the early show from the same date [19]
- Recommends also getting the late show from the same date [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-03-21.late.aud.lee.pcrp.21779.shnf**: taped by Recorded by Ken & Judy Lee on a Sony pc-124 cassette deck with Sony dynamic mics on Norelco cassettes. Microphones were set up in the balcony with a 10-20 foot spread.; transferred by John J Hance; source: Cassette Master> Soundforge> cd> SHN [1]. Also: Original tape was baked; shell replaced, then transferred with Tascam 122mk3 and Lucid ADA1000 to disc by John Jay Hance [1]
- **gd70-03-21.late.aud.5316.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Usher Tree; source: Audience - Late Show Only [5]. Also: Ken Lee is credited as responsible for most Capitol Theatre audience recordings [5]
- **gd70-03-21.early.aud.5315.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Usher Tree; source: Audience - Early Show Only [7]
- **gd70-03-21.early.lee.pcrp.20184.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Ken & Judy Lee; transferred by John Jay Hance, Peter G, Evan Bellaff; source: Audience - Early Show Only [8]
